evals.prompt: hey so our e2e tests in otaku-odyssey have gotten really out of hand. we have like 14000 tests and I want to know which ones are actually worth keeping vs deleting. we have this @oo/inventory package that catalogs all our pages and actions and permissions, and a playwright config with a bunch of projects. can you audit the suite and tell me what's redundant? i want numbers — like per-page ceilings, which modules have too many tests, which tests are duplicates, and which can move to vitest instead
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive categorization report with per-module analysis including spec counts vs ceilings, persona coverage ratios, action coverage gaps, duplicate test titles flagged, wave-directory candidates, and vitest migration candidates. Report written to docs/audit/ with consolidation candidates prioritized by effort.

evals.prompt: I need to figure out which tests are critical enough to run in cross-browser (firefox, webkit, mobile) vs just chromium. We have @critical tags on 213 files and that's way too many. Also some modules have way more tests than they should — staff-finance has 48 specs for 14 routes, that seems excessive. Can you apply some kind of methodology to categorize them into tiers?
evals.expected_output: Per-module analysis showing criticality tiers for each module. Specific recommendations for which @critical-tagged tests should remain cross-browser (layout/rendering risks) vs demote to chromium-only. Staff-finance analysis showing which 48 specs exceed the per-page ceiling and which business invariants justify the excess.

evals.prompt: our test categorization audit from last month found that every module exceeds its per-page ceiling and there are 94 test titles duplicated across files. we also have these test-wave directories (wave-1 through wave-7) that seem like historical artifacts. i need a prioritized action plan — what do i delete first? what's safe to remove without browser verification? and can you produce a json batch file i can feed to some ai classification agent?
evals.expected_output: Prioritized consolidation plan: P0 (entirely skipped files to remove now), P1 (duplicate test titles with canonical copies to deduplicate), P2 (wave-directory amortization candidates), P3 (vitest migration candidates). JSON classification batch file in docs/audit/ ready for Jev consumption. Conservative — when in doubt, retain.
